newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs stay high, some see firm week ahead.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs stay high, some see firm week ahead.

text.p: The very large crude carrier (VLCC) market enjoyed another busy week, with rates firming as a consequence, especially to eastern destinations, brokers said on Friday.
VLCCs to Japan hit the W80 mark, with South Korea not far behind at W78.5 and Singapore around W75. VLCCs to Europe were slightly up at about W65.

Brokers Galbraith's Ltd said, "Owners have certainly not seen a market like this for some time, and are generally feeling very punchy, trying to talk the market up and not showing much remorse if they miss out on a cargo..."
"We think the market still might have a little way to go for modern ships, with one or two Korean or Japanese charterers having to pay '80 something'.
"Otherwise the market looks like it might have peaked, but any fall will be slow and rates next week will probably be at similar levels."

Brokers E.A. Gibson said the total out of the Mideast Gulf was slightly up this week at 32 vessels totalling just over nine million tonnes. Of these, 19 ships, or 4.8 million tonnes, were chartered eastwards.
It was also a good week for ultra-large vessels (ULCCs), which achieved W75 to the Red Sea and W60 to the U.S. Gulf.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs edged up to W67.5 amid good demand, brokers said.

Suezmaxes (130,000 tonne vessels) were in the doldrums however, with rates flat to softer and charterers having a free hand in picking good quality, modern tonnage. West Africa/U.S. Gulf Suezmaxes were fixed at W82.5 or slightly less, while the Med was awash with tonnage with W85 the prevailing rate on Friday.
